summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause: President Trump and Secretary of State Rubio say new strikes are unlikely or not needed while the US blockade of Iran continues, and Qatar says it sees progress in mediation. Iran denies that talks are under way and says the Strait of Hormuz stays shut to unapproved shipping until its conditions are met; attacks on tankers in and near the strait continued on Nov 10, and Iran's army said a tanker caught fire in the strait after hitting a mine on Nov 11. On Nov 11 Iran's parliament speaker said the strait will never return to its pre-war status, while President Trump said the US has already won and wants a total victory. On Nov 12 Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi oil sites, and oil rose about 3%. On Nov 13 Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to an overnight strike on the Hormuz port town of Sirik; US Central Command denied it, saying US forces shot down two Iranian drones aimed at Bahrain with no injuries or damage. Brent was near US$96 on Friday, set for a second weekly fall.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are controlled by the US and its regional partners. Most traffic moves through a shuttle system the US coordinates with Arab partners, with weekly volumes swinging as attacks continue (Al Jazeera).

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: About 11.6 million barrels a day over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline (Kpler, via Al Jazeera).

status.label: The war
status.note: US officials said the US carried out limited, defensive strikes on Iranian targets, including on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz on Nov 2, after Iranian surface-to-air missile threats; they said it was not a resumption of major combat (Wall Street Journal, then Reuters). Indirect talks through Qatari mediators continue with no breakthrough announced; Vice President Vance said there has been progress. On Nov 7 the US carried out further strikes on Iranian air defences on Qeshm Island, which President Trump called minor (Euronews). On Nov 8 Trump told CNN renewed attacks were highly unlikely if talks make real progress; no deal has been signed.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Reuters reported on Friday, Nov 13, that Brent was near US$96 a barrel and set for a second weekly decline as the US kept its blockade of Iran instead of new strikes; on Thursday it had risen about 3% (Reuters via Yahoo Finance; RTE).

updates.text: US Central Command denied Iran's claim that a US radar in Bahrain was destroyed, saying US forces shot down two one-way attack drones launched by Iran's Revolutionary Guard toward Bahrain, with no injuries or damage.
sources: Fox News live: Iran rules out nuclear inspections while under threat from US

updates.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said, via state media, that it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain after an overnight strike on a telecom tower in Sirik, a port town on Iran's Hormuz coast; the US and Bahrain did not immediately comment, and the claim could not be independently verified.
sources: AP via ABC News: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it destroyed a US radar in Bahrain
RFE/RL: Iran claims strike on US radar in Bahrain after attack on Hormuz port town

updates.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said, via state media, that a tanker carrying LNG struck a naval mine and suffered an explosion in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday while using what it called an unauthorised route; Reuters reported no details on the tanker were immediately available.
sources: Reuters via Yahoo News: Iran says tanker carrying LNG hit mine, suffered explosion in Hormuz

updates.text: Reuters, citing three sources, reported that Iran attacked ship navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island in the Strait of Hormuz, which Iranian state media had claimed on Nov 10; shipping sources said the damage was unlikely to cause major disruption.
sources: Organiser (citing Reuters): Iran strikes Oman island navigation systems
Maritime Executive: Uncertainty surrounds possible attack on Oman's Strait of Hormuz lighthouse

updates.text: Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi oil and military sites on Nov 12, including the East-West pipeline and Yanbu oil facilities. Reuters reported that oil settled about US$3 higher on Thursday on attacks on Saudi energy sites and Strait of Hormuz disruptions.
sources: The New Arab: Yemen's Houthis claim attacks on Saudi oil, military sites
TASS: Houthis claim responsibility for strikes on Saudi Aramco, airbase in Saudi Arabia
Reuters via Yahoo Finance: Oil settles $3 higher on attacks on Saudi energy sites, Strait of Hormuz disruptions

updates.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two supertankers were disabled by explosions on Wednesday night after ignoring warnings against an unauthorised route, and Iran's army said two more tankers hit mines in the eastern strait on Thursday afternoon. Reuters said it could not immediately verify Iran's account; UKMTO reported a vessel hit by an unidentified projectile about 14 nautical miles northwest of Ras Al-Khaimah on Wednesday, with all crew evacuated.
sources: Reuters via GV Wire: Four tankers struck by explosions in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says
AFP via Gulf Today: Two oil tankers 'disabled' by explosions in Strait of Hormuz

updates.text: President Trump said on Nov 12 that the US does not need a deal with Iran; no agreement has been announced and the blockade continues.
sources: ABC News live: 'We don't need a deal with Iran,' Trump says
Haaretz: Trump says Iran deal is no longer needed

updates.text: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said on Nov 11 that the Strait of Hormuz will never return to its pre-war status and that Iran will not back down.
sources: Al Jazeera: Hormuz Strait will 'never return' to pre-war status, Iran's Ghalibaf says
Iran International live: Ghalibaf says Iran will not back down

updates.text: President Trump said on Nov 11 that the US has already won the war with Iran and that he wants a total victory; no agreement has been announced.
sources: Times of Israel live blog, Nov 11
Iran International live: Trump seeks 'total victory'

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
